articles.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
articles.summary: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry.
body: The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.

Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.
There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.

articles.title: Man Utd expected to back Poch in January transfer window
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as the club aim to address their disappointing start to the season.
body: A left-back, centre-back and forward are areas the club are looking to potentially strengthen in January with Pochettino expected to have input on targets they will pursue.

Despite the club's hierarchy feeling the team should be further up the table, there is also an acknowledgement that they could have further strengthened the squad in the summer in areas where they lacked depth.

Sky Sports News understands the club already had plans to move in the upcoming window under former head coach Michael Carrick, before he was sacked last month following United's worst start to a league season for 40 years.
However, Pochettino is now expected to be consulted in the coming weeks and will have his say on potential recruits in January.

articles.title: Ireland’s Prendergast free to face South Africa after avoiding hip-drop tackle ban
articles.summary: Fly-half was cited for alleged unlawful tackle against Fiji. Rassie Erasmus had predicted player would be cleared. Ireland’s fly-half Sam Prendergast is available to face South Africa in the Nations Championship on Saturday after his citing for an alleged hip-drop tackle against Fiji was dismissed.
body: Prendergast was cited for the challenge on Fiji’s captain Peceli Yato under a new offence added to Law 9.13 at the start of November. However, following a hearing on Tuesday, an independent disciplinary committee decided no further action would be taken against the 23-year-old, who could have been hit with a suspension.

South Africa’s head coach Rassie Erasmus had predicted Prendergast would avoid a suspension and be free to play against the Springboks. Erasmus has been handed a six-match ban, which takes immediate effect, after questioning whether the officiating during last Friday’s defeat by France amounted to match-fixing.

A statement from the Nations Championship read: “Sam Prendergast appeared before an independent disciplinary committee on Tuesday 17 November, having been cited for an alleged act of foul play contrary to Law 9.13 during the Nations Championship match between Ireland and Fiji on Saturday 14 November.

articles.title: Duckett’s bold 133 steers England to ODI series win as sandpapergate latest rocks Australia
articles.summary: As per Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, upon announcing the creation of a forum for players to share memories of sandpaper in South Africa eight years ago, two diametrically opposed versions of events can both be true.
body: By that logic, anyone remembering this deciding one-day international in Hobart as a win for Australia in years to come will not technically be wrong. It will simply be “their truth”, to use an overused phrase in this saga.

Back in the real world, however, on the day when Cameron Bancroft’s 4,000-word mea culpa implicated virtually Australia’s entire touring party back in 2018, the opposite was very much the case. Driven by Ben Duckett’s 115-ball 133, it was England who emerged victorious under lights by a margin of 97 runs.

First came a helter-skelter charge to 328 all out in 48.3 overs, with Duckett’s flurry of 15 fours and three sixes augmented by a critical half-century from Will Jacks at the back end. Then came a charge with the ball similar to Adelaide, culminating in Australia’s collapse to 231 all out on the banks of the Derwent Estuary.

A 2-1 series win for Harry Brook’s tourists, therefore, and a low-key encouraging one, too. Admittedly the hosts were without Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc – a penny for their thoughts right now – but this was still the first time England had come from behind to claim an ODI series in Australia.

articles.title: Explosive Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins
articles.summary: Cameron Bancroft claims the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 sandpaper plot in explosive revelations that will heap pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.
body: In a detailed testimony, published by the West Australian,, external batter Bancroft - the player caught with the sandpaper during the Test match against South Africa - has given arguably the most complete account of the events in Cape Town eight years ago.
"In 2018 not the entire truth was told," said Bancroft. "I have never been completely honest about what happened."
For the past two weeks, Australian cricket has been embroiled in a debate over the ball-tampering saga following the publication of Usman Khawaja's autobiography.
Khawaja wrote that the whole Australia team knew of the plot, claims supported by David Warner and Chadd Sayers. Cummins described Khawaja's account as "wrong" and "nonsense".

articles.title: England cruise to ODI series win over Australia
articles.summary: England secured a come-from-behind ODI series win over Australia as Ben Duckett's century and Sonny Baker's new-ball wickets teed up a thumping 97-run victory in the Hobart decider.
body: Harry Brook's side had been skittled for 131 in Perth on Friday en route to slipping 1-0 down in the three-match contest but rallied in Adelaide on Sunday with a 135-run triumph before this convincing result at Ninja Stadium.
Australia were shot out for 231 chasing 329 on Wednesday, with Brook taking the final wicket of tailender Spencer Johnson.

Wednesday's win, England's first over Australia in Hobart, was similar to their success at the weekend: a total above 300 underpinned by a century from an opener - Ben Duckett here after Tom Banton in Adelaide - proved too much for the hosts, whose top order struggled once more when looking to drive.

After Duckett's 133, his seventh ODI ton and first outside England and Pakistan, helped propel his side from 195-5 to 328 all out in 48.3 overs, Australia plummeted to 5-2 and 34-3 in reply - Baker (4-45) nicking off Mitch Marsh (1) and Josh Inglis (14) with out-swingers.

articles.title: Opetaia out of Wilder fight on Fury-Joshua card
articles.summary: Australian Jai Opetaia withdraws from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua in December.
body: Australian Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua.
Unbeaten cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia was set to step up to heavyweight for the first time to face American Wilder at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.
Opetaia, 31, did not give a reason for his withdrawal, but it is understood he aggravated a hand injury in training.
"Apologies to everyone and especially [Wilder] and his team for withdrawing from the bout," he wrote on Instagram.

articles.title: Former Spain midfielder Mata retires aged 38
articles.summary: Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata, who had spells at Chelsea and Manchester United in the Premier League, announces his retirement from playing at the age of 38.
body: Mata, who made 41 international appearances, was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup, and he helped his country win the European Championship two years later when he scored in the 4-0 final victory against Italy.
A former Real Madrid youth player, he joined Valencia in 2007 before a move to Chelsea in August 2011 where he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup.
Mata moved to Manchester United in January 2014 and helped them claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup prior to his departure in 2022.
He went on to have spells at Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

articles.title: What does Arteta do with Konsa once Saliba returns?
articles.summary: Arsenal have a big set of fixtures coming up after the November international break. Big games require big team selections - and Mikel Arteta has a huge decision to make in his defence.
body: William Saliba is coming back, which is a major boost for the Premier League champions, but to say Arsenal have missed him in recent weeks has been an understatement. Ezri Konsa has stepped up.

Not only has Konsa stepped in brilliantly for the injured Frenchman, but he has even proven to be just as good as Saliba was in Arsenal's title-winning season. Some areas of the data show Konsa has performed at higher levels.

But with Saliba now back in training and stepping up his fitness, Arteta has a task to balance the reintegration of one of his most important players, whilst keeping arguably their most in-form player happy.
And given the likes of Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Tottenham, Real Madrid and Manchester United face the Gunners before Christmas, these calls are important.

articles.title: NI will carry momentum into Euro 2028 qualifiers
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says his Nations League promotion winners will plot their next 12 months after the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in December.
body: Speaking before his side ground out the required point against Hungary to seal top spot in Nations League Group B2, Northern Ireland's Trai Hume told reporters that automatic promotion had not been the most immediate aim coming into the campaign.
Two years ago, this side were a League C team, battling to return to the second tier from a group containing Belarus, Bulgaria and Luxembourg.

Fast forward 24 months and a League A place was secured on the final night of an unbeaten campaign that had looked a serious challenge. Prior the trip to Georgia in September, Northern Ireland had a record of played 10, lost eight and drawn two at this level.

Across six games in eight weeks, the side won three and drew three, conceding just once along the way. Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser in Budapest on Tuesday secured the draw required to top the group and earn promotion to the top tier for the first time.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama’s ridiculous self-assisted dunk steals the show despite Spurs’ 105-93 loss to Pistons
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama produced another highlight-reel moment against the Detroit Pistons, throwing the ball off the backboard before catching it and finishing with a one-handed dunk.
body: The San Antonio Spurs star used his incredible height and creativity to get past Ausar Thompson early in their meeting with Detroit.
Wembanyama had already been blocked by one of the Thompson twins this season, but he found a different way to attack the basket this time.

The 22-year-old drove towards the paint just over a minute into the game before sensing pressure from Thompson. Rather than force his way through the defence, Wembanyama threw the ball against the backboard, collected it in the air and threw down a one-handed finish.

It was a reminder of the unusual skills that make the Frenchman such a difficult player to defend. At 7-foot-4, Wembanyama has the size to dominate near the rim, but his ability to improvise makes him even more dangerous.

articles.title: Greenwich holds off Ridgefield for 4th straight Class LL girls swimming title, 33rd overall
articles.summary: WEST HARTFORD - The Greenwich and Ridgefield girls swimming and diving programs have engaged in plenty of battles over the years, and the CIAC Class LL championship meet on Tuesday night at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center was no different.
body: For the Cardinals, depth turned out to be key as they captured their fourth straight Class LL title and 33rd overall in program history. Greenwich scored 924 points to second-place Ridgefield's 878.5. Amity was third with 510.5 points.
"I felt pretty confident going into this because I knew that everyone on the team has been working super hard, and I had a lot of faith in us," Greenwich junior Olivia DeVries said.

With sophomore Alden Charette's first-place finish in Class LL diving, the Cardinals won three individual events and one relay. Seniors Kensie Worden (50 freestyle, 23.59) and Julia Kozma (100 butterfly, 57.70) won gold medals, as did the opening 200 medley relay team of Charette, junior Sara Jee, Kozma and Worden (1:47.96).
Greenwich claimed 18 individual medals, including three golds, three silvers and three bronzes. DeVries claimed bronze medals in the 200 freestyle and 500 freestyle.
